title: A Library That Lends Tools
subtitle: 社区与资源 · 原创短文与原文定位
body: When a small town library began lending tools as well as books, several residents worried that broken equipment would cost more to replace than the new service could possibly save for local residents. The librarian therefore started with basic items, such as hammers and measuring tapes, which volunteers could inspect easily before each borrower took them home for a weekend project. Although some people initially borrowed equipment because they wanted to spend less, they later said that advice from other borrowers was an equally valuable part of visiting the library. At the end of the trial, the town decided to keep the service small until it understood how much staff time was required to make every loan safe and useful.
translation:
当一座小镇图书馆开始同时出借工具和书籍时，一些居民担心，更换损坏设备的成本可能超过这项新服务带来的节约。
因此，馆员从锤子、卷尺等基础物品开始，这些物品容易由志愿者在借用者带回家做周末项目之前检查。
尽管一些人最初借设备是为了省钱，他们后来表示，其他借用者的建议同样是到访图书馆的重要收获。
试行结束后，小镇决定保持服务规模较小，直到弄清要让每次借用安全且有用究竟需要多少员工时间。

title: The Bus Stop Experiment
subtitle: 交通与日常 · 原创短文与原文定位
body: Because passengers at a suburban bus stop could not tell whether a bus had already left, many arrived much earlier than necessary and spent uncomfortable mornings waiting beside a busy road. Instead of immediately buying an electronic display, the transport team posted a clear timetable and asked drivers to report the delays that occurred repeatedly during the same part of the morning. What surprised the team was that a delivery truck, which blocked a narrow turning area twice a week, explained several of the longest delays recorded during the short observation period. Once the delivery time was changed, journeys became more predictable, but the team kept collecting reports because a solution that worked in spring might not work when winter traffic increased.
translation:
由于郊区一个公交站的乘客无法判断公交车是否已经离开，许多人到得过早，在繁忙道路旁不舒服地等待。
交通团队没有立即购买电子显示屏，而是张贴清晰的时刻表，并让司机报告每天早晨同一时段反复出现的延误。
让团队惊讶的是，一辆每周两次挡住狭窄转弯区域的送货车解释了短期观察中数次最长的延误。
送货时间调整后，行程更可预测，但团队继续收集报告，因为春季有效的办法未必在冬季车流增加时有效。

title: A Garden Above the Street
subtitle: 城市与环境 · 原创短文与原文定位
body: After the owner of an apartment building offered residents an unused roof, a group of neighbours proposed a garden that would provide herbs while giving people a reason to meet outdoors. Before anyone carried soil upstairs, however, an engineer checked the roof because the weight of wet planting containers could be much greater than the residents had expected from looking at empty pots. The final plan used fewer containers than the group had imagined, but it included wide paths so that residents who used walking aids could reach the plants without difficulty. By sharing watering duties and recording which plants survived the windy conditions, the neighbours gradually created a space whose value depended as much on cooperation as on the amount of food produced.

一栋公寓的业主向住户提供闲置屋顶后，一群邻居提议建花园，既种香草，也让大家有理由到户外见面。

最终方案使用的种植箱比小组原想的少，但加入宽通道，让使用助行器的居民也能方便地接近植物。

title: Repair Before Replacement
subtitle: 消费与维修 · 原创短文与原文定位
body: When her headphones stopped producing sound in one ear, Maya assumed that replacing them would be easier than finding someone who could identify a fault inside such a small device. At a neighbourhood repair event, a volunteer showed her that the problem was a loose connection near the cable, rather than damage to the expensive components hidden inside the plastic case. Although the repair took less than an hour, the volunteer explained that opening another model might be difficult if its parts were glued together instead of being held with removable screws. Maya left with working headphones and a different question for her next purchase: whether the manufacturer provided spare parts and instructions that would make a future repair reasonably possible.
translation:
耳机一边不出声时，Maya 认为买新的比找到能查出小设备内部故障的人更容易。
在社区维修活动上，志愿者告诉她，问题是线缆附近的连接松了，并不是塑料外壳内部昂贵零件损坏。
尽管维修不到一小时，志愿者解释说，如果另一款耳机的零件是粘接而非用可拆螺丝固定，拆开可能很困难。
Maya 带着修好的耳机离开，也为下次购物准备了不同的问题：厂家是否提供能让日后维修切实可行的备件和说明。

title: The Quiet Hour
subtitle: 公共空间 · 原创短文与原文定位
body: A museum introduced a quiet visiting hour after families explained that bright screens and sudden sounds sometimes made it difficult for children to stay long enough to enjoy the exhibits. During that hour, staff lowered the volume of recordings, provided a simple map of calm areas, and allowed visitors to leave a room and return without having to explain their reasons. The changes did not remove every source of discomfort, and the museum avoided claiming that one arrangement could meet the needs of all people who experienced the building differently. Instead, visitors could send short comments after their visit, which helped staff decide where a clearer sign or a more predictable sound would be more useful than another general rule.
translation:
一些家庭反映亮屏和突然的声音会让孩子难以停留足够久欣赏展品后，博物馆推出了安静参观时段。
在该时段，员工降低录音音量，提供安静区域简图，并允许参观者离开房间后再返回，无需解释理由。

title: Labels That Tell the Truth
subtitle: 食物与信息 · 原创短文与原文定位
body: When a campus café labelled a sandwich as local, a student asked whether the word described the bread, the vegetables, or simply the building in which the ingredients had been assembled. The manager discovered that the supplier had used a broad definition, under which products counted as local even if only the final preparation had taken place within the nearby region. Rather than remove all information from the menu, the café began listing where its main ingredients came from and noted that availability could change when weather interrupted the usual deliveries. Customers still had to decide what mattered to them, but the more precise description allowed those who valued regional farming to make choices without relying on a word that concealed important differences.

title: A Screen-Free Table
subtitle: 注意与习惯 · 原创短文与原文定位
body: At the start of each shared dinner, four housemates placed their phones on a shelf because they wanted to find out whether a small change could make their conversations less fragmented. They agreed that anyone expecting an urgent call could keep a phone nearby, since a rule that ignored real responsibilities would be unlikely to last beyond the first inconvenient evening. After two weeks, the group reported longer conversations, although they also recognised that paying unusual attention to the experiment might have influenced how much effort they made to talk. Instead of presenting their experience as proof about everyone, they kept the arrangement because it suited their household and revisited it whenever a change in work schedules made dinner harder to organise.

两周后，小组说谈话变长了，但他们也承认，对实验格外关注可能影响了自己投入交谈的努力。

title: The Second-Hand Desk
subtitle: 设计与循环 · 原创短文与原文定位
body: A student who needed a desk for a small bedroom found a used one online, but she asked for its measurements before arranging collection because photographs often made furniture appear smaller. When she visited the seller, she noticed a damaged drawer that had not been shown clearly, so she discussed a lower price rather than assuming the entire desk was unusable. Her friend helped replace the drawer handle, while a local workshop cut a narrow shelf from a piece of leftover wood that would otherwise have been discarded after another project. The desk was not the cheapest option once transport and repairs were included, yet the student valued its sturdy construction and the fact that its parts could be changed separately.

见卖家时，她发现一个未被清楚拍出的坏抽屉，于是商量降价，而没有认定整张桌子都不能用。

title: A Route with Shade
subtitle: 健康与城市 · 原创短文与原文定位
body: During a hot week, a community walking group changed its usual route after members said that a shorter distance was not necessarily easier when most of the path remained exposed to direct sunlight. The organiser marked benches, drinking fountains, and shaded sections on a paper map, which allowed walkers to choose places to pause without feeling that they were interrupting the entire group. Although the new route took longer, several members preferred it because they could talk comfortably and decide for themselves whether to complete the whole walk or return from an earlier turning point. The group did not treat the map as medical advice; it was simply a practical record of local conditions that each person could combine with their own needs and any professional guidance.
translation:
炎热的一周里，社区步行小组改变常用路线，因为成员表示，如果大部分路面暴晒，距离较短未必更轻松。
组织者把长椅、饮水点和阴凉路段标在纸地图上，让步行者能自行选地方暂停，不必觉得自己打断了整个队伍。
新路线耗时更长，但一些成员更喜欢，因为能舒适交谈，并自行决定走完全程还是从较早的转弯点返回。
小组没把地图当医疗建议，它只是当地条件的实用记录，每个人可结合自身需要及专业指导使用。

Instead of forcing every step into a fixed measurement, she recorded a conversation in which he described how the colour changed and why he added water whenever the weather was dry. The written version still included approximate quantities, because a cousin who had never made the dish needed a starting point before learning to recognise the signs that experienced cooks noticed naturally. title: A Photograph without a Date
subtitle: 历史与证据 · 原创短文与原文定位
body: While sorting through a box of old photographs, a local historian found an image of a crowded market that looked familiar, although nobody had written a date or location on the back. A shop sign in the background suggested one possible street, but the historian checked old business directories before accepting the identification because the same shop name had appeared in several districts. When two residents offered different memories of the scene, she recorded both accounts rather than choosing the story that sounded more confident or happened to fit her first impression of the picture. The final exhibition described the location as probable and explained the evidence that remained uncertain, allowing visitors to understand how historical conclusions can be revised when another useful source becomes available.

整理旧照片时，一位地方史研究者发现一张似曾相识的拥挤市场照片，但背面没有日期或地点。

title: The Cost of Free Delivery
subtitle: 商业与选择 · 原创短文与原文定位
body: A student ordering one notebook noticed that the online store offered free delivery only when the total purchase reached an amount that was considerably higher than the price of the item she needed. She added two small products to her basket before realising that the money spent to avoid the delivery charge exceeded what she would have paid if she had bought the notebook alone. The store had not hidden its prices, yet the phrase free delivery had drawn attention away from the total cost, which was the number that mattered for her limited weekly budget. After removing the extra items, she saved the delivery threshold in her notes so that she could combine future necessary purchases, provided that waiting would not create a different inconvenience or expense.

title: A Meeting with an Agenda
subtitle: 工作与沟通 · 原创短文与原文定位
body: After a student organisation spent three meetings discussing the same event without making a decision, its secretary suggested that each future meeting should begin with a short list of questions requiring answers. Members received the list in advance, which gave those who preferred to think quietly enough time to prepare their ideas instead of competing to speak before they had considered the options. During the next meeting, the chair separated questions that needed a decision from updates that could be read later, while a shared note recorded the reasons behind each agreement rather than only its outcome. The new approach did not eliminate disagreement, but it made unfinished decisions visible so that members knew what evidence to bring when an issue returned to the agenda in the following week.

学生组织开了三次会仍未决定同一活动后，秘书建议以后每次会议先列出需要回答的简短问题清单。

下次开会时，主持人区分需决定的问题与可稍后阅读的进展；共享记录记下每项决定的理由，而不只写结果。

title: Numbers on a Fitness Watch
subtitle: 数据与判断 · 原创短文与原文定位
body: When Arun began using a fitness watch, he treated every daily number as a precise description of his activity until a long bus journey was partly counted as walking by the device. The unexpected result encouraged him to read the product guide, which explained that movement estimates depended on sensor signals and could be affected by activities that resembled the motion of a person's arm. He still found the watch useful for noticing broad patterns, but he stopped comparing tiny differences between days as if each extra step represented a meaningful change in his overall physical condition. title: The Last Shelf in the Fridge
subtitle: 家庭与浪费 · 原创短文与原文定位
body: Three housemates discovered that food was often thrown away because each person assumed the vegetables on the lowest shelf belonged to someone else and avoided using them even when they were nearly spoiled. They placed a small basket on that shelf for ingredients that anyone could use, and the owner of each item wrote a date indicating when it had been opened or cooked. Because sharing labels could not make unsafe food safe, the group also agreed to follow storage instructions and discard anything that showed clear signs of deterioration rather than treating the basket as a rescue for every leftover. After several weeks, their shopping list became shorter because they checked the basket before buying more, although they could not tell how much of the change came from paying closer attention generally.

三位室友发现食物常被扔掉，因为大家都以为底层蔬菜属于别人，即使快坏了也不敢用。

title: Learning to Ask Better Questions
subtitle: 学习与探究 · 原创短文与原文定位
body: A tutor noticed that students often said they did not understand an article, although their difficulties ranged from one unfamiliar word to uncertainty about how the author's evidence supported the final conclusion. She invited each learner to point to a particular sentence and explain what had seemed clear just before the confusion began, which helped turn a general feeling of failure into a specific question. For one student, drawing a line between a claim and the paragraph that justified it revealed a missing connection, while another needed a simple explanation of a word used in an unusual sense. The tutor did not require a perfect question before offering help, but she encouraged students to notice where understanding changed so that their next request could guide a more useful conversation about the text.
translation:
导师发现学生常说“不懂文章”，但困难其实从一个生词到不明白证据如何支持结论，各不相同。
她请每位学习者指出具体句子，并解释困惑之前哪些内容是清楚的，把笼统的失败感变成具体问题。
对一名学生而言，把论点连到支持它的段落揭示了缺失联系；另一人则需要解释某个词不常见的含义。
导师不要求先提出完美问题才帮忙，但鼓励学生留意理解在哪里发生变化，让下次求助促成更有用的文本讨论。

title: An App with Fewer Alerts
subtitle: 科技与注意 · 原创短文与原文定位
body: A small software team received complaints that its planning app interrupted users too frequently, even though each notification had originally been added because someone believed the information would be useful at that moment. Instead of asking users to disable every alert separately, the designers grouped notifications by purpose and offered a quiet default that people could change after seeing a clear example of what each option meant. Important reminders remained available for people who wanted them, while routine summaries were moved into the app so that opening a planning tool did not automatically create more messages throughout the rest of the day. The team evaluated the redesign through voluntary feedback and observed settings changes, recognising that a lower number of notifications alone could not prove that users felt calmer or completed more meaningful work.

title: A Shop That Closes Earlier
subtitle: 工作与生活 · 原创短文与原文定位
body: When a bookshop owner considered closing an hour earlier on weekdays, she worried that customers who came after work would lose their only convenient opportunity to browse the shelves and collect their orders. Rather than change every evening at once, she tested the shorter schedule on two quiet days and offered a secure collection arrangement for customers whose orders had already been paid for online. Staff reported that the new schedule made transport home easier, but the owner also recorded missed collections and unanswered requests because benefits for employees did not remove the need to understand effects on customers. At the end of the trial, she kept one late evening each week and published the different hours clearly, choosing a compromise that reflected the shop's actual patterns rather than a universal rule about retail.

title: The Missing Context of a Chart
subtitle: 媒体与统计 · 原创短文与原文定位
body: A newspaper chart showed that bicycle thefts had risen sharply in one district, leading some readers to assume that cycling there had become much riskier than it had been in the previous year. A closer look revealed that the district had also installed many more parking spaces and attracted a larger number of cyclists, information that was absent from the dramatic headline printed above the chart. This did not mean that the theft problem was unimportant, but it meant that total incidents and the chance of a particular parked bicycle being stolen were different questions requiring different kinds of evidence. The reporter updated the story to include both counts and available parking data, while explaining that incomplete information about actual bicycle use prevented a confident estimate of how individual risk had changed.

报纸图表显示某区自行车失窃大增，让一些读者以为在那里骑车比前一年危险很多。
仔细看发现，该区也新增了许多停车位并吸引更多骑行者，而这些信息没出现在图表上方醒目的标题中。
这不意味着失窃不重要，而是说总事件数与一辆具体停放自行车的失窃概率是不同问题，需要不同证据。
记者更新报道，加入事件数及可得停车数据，同时说明实际使用数据不完整，无法有把握估计个人风险如何变化。

title: The Value of a Waiting List
subtitle: 社区与分配 · 原创短文与原文定位
body: A popular community pottery class filled within minutes of registration opening, which meant that people who could not check their phones during working hours rarely had an opportunity to attend the monthly sessions. The organiser introduced a waiting list and reserved a few places for first-time participants, explaining the process publicly so that a change intended to improve access would not appear to depend on personal connections. When a registered learner cancelled, the next person received a message with enough time to respond, rather than losing the place immediately because a second applicant happened to answer more quickly. The revised system could not create unlimited places, but it made the rules easier to understand and gave the organiser better information about how many additional sessions might be useful in the future.

社区陶艺课报名几分钟就满，导致工作时不能看手机的人几乎没机会参加每月课程。
组织者引入候补名单，为初次参加者保留少量名额，并公开流程，避免改善机会的改变被误解为依靠关系。

title: A Park after Dark
subtitle: 自然与照明 · 原创短文与原文定位
body: Residents living beside a small park requested brighter lights after several people said that the path felt difficult to follow at night, especially where tree branches covered the existing lamps during the summer. Before adding new equipment everywhere, the council asked a lighting specialist to examine whether better positioning and clearer path edges could improve visibility while reducing unnecessary light directed towards nearby bedroom windows. An ecologist also advised leaving one area darker because insects and other animals used the vegetation there, although the team needed further observation before claiming that any particular design would protect local wildlife. The completed plan used directed lighting along the main route and invited feedback from evening walkers, treating safety, residents' comfort, and the surrounding habitat as concerns that had to be considered together.

title: The Promise of a Seed Library
subtitle: 种植与分享 · 原创短文与原文定位
body: A seed library invited gardeners to take small packets in spring and return seeds after harvest, hoping that the exchange would help neighbours try varieties they might not find in ordinary shops. The coordinator soon learned that saving suitable seeds required more knowledge than some beginners expected, because certain plants could cross with nearby varieties or produce seeds that did not grow reliably the following year. Instead of rejecting all contributions that lacked perfect records, volunteers offered workshops and asked donors to note where the plants had grown, when seeds were collected, and anything unusual they had observed. Packets were labelled with the information available rather than a promise of guaranteed results, allowing the library to encourage experimentation while remaining honest about the limits of an exchange run by local volunteers.

title: When a Translation Needs a Reader
subtitle: 语言与沟通 · 原创短文与原文定位
body: A volunteer translating a museum leaflet realised that a sentence which sounded elegant in the original language became confusing when every phrase was moved into English in exactly the same order. She first identified the information a visitor needed, such as where to enter and which rooms required a separate ticket, before deciding how to express those details in clear and natural sentences. Although a colleague suggested replacing unfamiliar cultural terms with familiar ones, she kept several original names and added short explanations because an easy comparison could sometimes hide a distinction that mattered. After two readers tested the leaflet by following its instructions, their questions helped her revise the wording, showing that a translation can require careful attention to practical use as well as grammatical accuracy.
translation:
志愿者翻译博物馆折页时发现，原文优美的句子若每个短语都按原顺序转成英语，就会让人困惑。
她先确定访客需要的信息，如入口与哪些房间另收费，再决定如何用清晰自然的句子表达。
虽然同事建议用熟悉词替换陌生文化词，她保留了一些原名并补简短解释，因为简单类比有时会掩盖重要区别。
两位读者按折页指示试走后，他们的问题帮助她改措辞，说明翻译既需语法准确，也需留意实际用途。

title: The Shared Laundry Calendar
subtitle: 协作与安排 · 原创短文与原文定位
body: In a building with only two washing machines, neighbours often arrived with full baskets only to discover that both machines were running and that nobody knew when the next opportunity would appear. A resident proposed an online booking calendar, but the group kept a paper version near the laundry because several older neighbours preferred not to create another account simply to wash their clothes. Bookings were limited to one session at a time, and unused reservations expired after a short grace period so that a person who forgot an appointment would not block the machines for an entire evening. The calendar reduced uncertainty rather than creating more washing capacity, which meant the residents still needed to discuss busy weekends and agree on considerate ways of handling clothes that had been left behind.

只有两台洗衣机的楼里，邻居常提满篮衣物到场才发现都在使用，而且没人知道何时轮到自己。
一位住户提议网上预约，但大家也在洗衣间保留纸质版本，因为几位年长邻居不想为洗衣再建账号。
每人一次只能预约一场，未用预约过短暂宽限期就失效，避免忘记预约的人占住整个晚间。
日历减少的是不确定性，并没有增加洗衣容量，因此居民仍需商量忙碌周末及妥善处理遗留衣物的方法。

title: A Shorter Survey
subtitle: 研究与反馈 · 原创短文与原文定位
body: A university club sent members a long survey about its activities, but only a small fraction completed it, leaving the organisers unsure whether the answers represented the wider group or mainly its most enthusiastic participants. For the next event, they asked three focused questions and offered an optional space for comments, explaining how the responses would influence choices about timing, accessibility, and the type of activity offered. More people responded to the shorter form, although the organisers recognised that those who had stopped attending altogether might still be missing from the results and could have different reasons for staying away. When publishing the summary, they stated how many members had replied and avoided describing the most common answer as everyone's preference, keeping the difference between useful feedback and complete representation visible to readers.

大学社团发了长问卷，但只有少数完成，组织者无法确定结果代表全体还是主要代表最热情的成员。

短表收到更多回应，但组织者认识到，完全不来的人可能仍未被覆盖，而他们缺席的原因可能不同。

title: A Book Club Changes Pace
subtitle: 阅读与参与 · 原创短文与原文定位
body: A book club noticed that several members had become quiet during discussions, not because they disliked the books but because their work schedules left too little time to finish a long novel before each meeting. The organiser suggested alternating full books with shorter pieces, and members agreed that anyone could discuss the part they had read without apologising for the pages that remained unfinished at the end of the week. To avoid revealing important endings unexpectedly, participants placed a small marker on the shared reading schedule to show how far each discussion would go, which made it easier for newcomers to join with confidence. The group kept choosing challenging writing as well as accessible stories, since a welcoming pace did not require removing difficult ideas but did require giving people a reasonable way to approach them together.

title: Choosing a Reusable Cup
subtitle: 环境与条件 · 原创短文与原文定位
body: At a campus stall, a volunteer was asked whether buying a reusable cup was always better for the environment, a question that could not be answered carefully by comparing the materials of two cups alone. She explained that manufacturing, transport, washing, and the number of times an item was actually used could all affect its overall impact, which meant that ownership by itself was not the same as repeated use. Rather than recommend that everyone immediately buy a new product, the stall encouraged students to use suitable cups they already owned and to check whether nearby cafés accepted them under their current hygiene procedures. The discussion shifted from finding a product with a perfect label to building a practical routine, while recognising that different materials and local conditions would require more detailed evidence before making a precise environmental comparison.
translation:
校园摊位上，有人问志愿者可重复杯是否总更环保；只比较两个杯子的材料无法谨慎回答。
她解释，生产、运输、清洗和实际使用次数都会影响整体环境代价，拥有本身不等于重复使用。
摊位没有建议人人马上买新品，而是鼓励用已有合适杯子，并确认附近咖啡馆现行卫生流程是否接受自带杯。
讨论从找“完美标签”产品转向建立实用习惯，同时承认精确环境比较仍需不同材料与当地条件的更细证据。

title: A Map Made by Residents
subtitle: 地图与经验 · 原创短文与原文定位
body: An official neighbourhood map showed roads and public buildings clearly, but it did not indicate the steep steps, narrow gates, or uneven surfaces that could turn a short journey into a difficult one. A group of residents began recording these details during ordinary trips, marking observations with dates so that a broken surface which had later been repaired would not remain on the map as a permanent obstacle. They invited people with different needs to review the descriptions, because a route described as easy by a fast walker might be exhausting for someone carrying groceries or pushing a heavy child's buggy uphill. The finished map did not promise that every path would suit every visitor; instead, it provided specific information that people could combine with their own experience when deciding which way to travel through the area.

官方社区地图清楚标道路和公共建筑，却未标陡台阶、窄门、不平路面，而这些可能使短行程变困难。
居民在日常出行时开始记录细节并标日期，以免后来修好的破损路面仍被当作永久障碍。
他们请不同需求的人审核描述，因为快步行者觉得轻松的路线，对提菜或推重婴儿车上坡的人可能很累。

title: A Small Grant with a Clear Purpose
subtitle: 项目与决策 · 原创短文与原文定位
body: A student team received a small grant to improve a shared study room, but its first list of ideas included so many attractive features that the available money could not cover even half of them. Before voting for favourite products, the team asked regular users what prevented them from studying comfortably, discovering that poor desk lighting and too few power sockets mattered more than the proposed decorative wall. An electrician checked which changes could be made safely within the budget, while the students set aside a modest amount for repairs so that a single broken fixture would not leave them without resources later. The final report explained why several appealing ideas had been postponed, making it possible for the next team to revisit them if new funding arrived instead of repeating the same discussion from the beginning.

title: An Unusual Word in a Familiar Story
subtitle: 词汇与语境 · 原创短文与原文定位
body: While reading a newspaper article, Nia recognised every word in a sentence yet still misunderstood it because she had learned only the most common meaning of a verb that was being used differently. Instead of copying the first dictionary definition into her notebook, she compared several examples and noticed that the nouns surrounding the verb helped identify which meaning fitted the situation described by the writer. Her note included the original phrase and a short explanation in her own words, followed by a new sentence that she checked against a reliable reference rather than assuming any grammatically possible combination would sound natural. When she met the verb again in another text, she tried to infer its meaning before opening her notes, using the second encounter as an opportunity to test understanding rather than merely recognise the spelling.

Nia 读报时认识句中每个词却仍误解，因为她只学过一个动词最常见的意思，而文中用了另一义项。

title: A Holiday without a Full Schedule
subtitle: 旅行与节奏 · 原创短文与原文定位
body: Before a short visit to a coastal town, two friends listed so many attractions that moving between them would have occupied most of each day, leaving little time to enjoy the places themselves. They revised the plan by choosing one main activity for each morning and keeping the afternoons flexible, which allowed them to respond to changing weather without feeling that the whole trip had failed. When a ferry was cancelled, they visited a small local exhibition recommended by their host, although they checked its opening hours rather than assuming that every attraction would follow the same schedule as a major museum. Their final memories included an unplanned conversation with a fisherman and a slow lunch overlooking the harbour, reminding them that a useful itinerary can provide direction without deciding how every available minute must be spent.

去海边小镇短游前，两位朋友列太多景点，以至于每天大半时间要花在转场，几乎没空享受景点本身。
他们改成每早一项主活动、下午灵活，使天气变化时可调整而不觉得整趟旅行失败。
渡轮取消后，他们参观住处主人推荐的小展览，但先查开放时间，没有假设所有景点都按大型博物馆时间开门。

title: Who Is Missing from the Interview?
subtitle: 研究与包容 · 原创短文与原文定位
body: A design team interviewed regular visitors to a sports centre and heard many positive comments, but one researcher asked whether speaking only to current users could explain why some neighbours never entered the building. The next round included people who had considered joining but had not done so, revealing concerns about opening times, unclear pricing, and the impression that beginners would not know where to start. These interviews did not establish how common each concern was across the whole neighbourhood, since the participants had been recruited through a few local organisations rather than selected from a complete list of residents. Nevertheless, the comments identified practical changes worth testing, including a clearer welcome page and an introductory session, while leaving the team responsible for checking whether those changes actually improved access for the intended people.

设计团队访问运动中心常客，听到许多赞许，但研究者问，只访现有用户能否解释一些邻居从不进入的原因。
下一轮包括考虑加入却没加入的人，揭示开放时间、价格不清及新手不知从何开始的担忧。
访谈未确定每种担忧在全社区多常见，因为参与者来自少数机构招募，而非全体居民名单抽样。
尽管如此，意见指出值得测试的改变，如更清楚的欢迎页和入门活动；团队仍须检查是否真改善了目标人群的机会。

title: When a Shortcut Becomes a Detour
subtitle: 导航与判断 · 原创短文与原文定位
body: A navigation app directed a cyclist through a narrow lane because the route was slightly shorter, but the cyclist discovered that several gates and rough surfaces made the journey slower than the main road would have been. The app's distance calculation was not necessarily wrong; rather, the information it used did not fully describe the practical conditions that mattered to someone travelling with a heavy bag and a bicycle instead of a car. After reporting the problem, the cyclist saved a note about the lane and checked the broader map before future trips, especially when an unfamiliar shortcut passed through an area with few alternative exits. She continued using navigation as a source of guidance, while remembering that a recommendation based on limited data should be combined with signs, current conditions, and reasonable judgement about the kind of journey being made.

导航为骑行者选更短小路，但多道门和粗糙路面让旅途比主路更慢。
距离计算未必错，只是所用信息未充分描述一个背重包骑车者关心的实际条件。
反馈问题后，骑行者记下小路情况，以后出发前看更大范围地图，尤其陌生近道经过出口少的区域时。

title: The Translation of a Public Sign
subtitle: 语言与服务 · 原创短文与原文定位

title: A Student Newspaper Corrects a Story
subtitle: 媒体与责任 · 原创短文与原文定位
body: After a student newspaper reported that a campus café would close permanently, its editor learned that the café was actually shutting for repairs and expected to reopen once work on the damaged kitchen had been completed. The original reporter had relied on a notice saying closed until further notice, interpreting uncertainty about a date as evidence that the business would never return to the same location again in the future. Rather than quietly changing the article and leaving readers unaware of the error, the editor added a visible correction that explained what had been wrong and linked to the café's updated statement about the planned repairs. At the next editorial meeting, the team discussed how to distinguish an absence of information from confirmation of a specific outcome, treating the mistake as a reason to improve its verification process rather than conceal uncertainty.

title: A Device Designed for Repair
subtitle: 技术与设计 · 原创短文与原文定位
body: An engineering class was asked to design a desk lamp that could be repaired with ordinary tools, which changed the students' priorities before they had even chosen the shape of its shade or base. Instead of hiding every connection beneath a sealed cover, one team used visible screws and labelled wires so that someone opening the lamp later could understand how its parts were meant to fit together. Their first prototype was slightly larger than a competing design, but the team argued that a smaller object was not automatically better if a minor fault would make the entire product impossible to service safely. During testing, another student followed the repair instructions without help, revealing where a diagram was unclear and reminding the designers that replaceable parts were useful only when people could actually reach and identify them.

一组未将连接全封住，而用可见螺丝和标记电线，让日后打开的人了解零件如何连接。
首个原型比竞争设计稍大，但团队说若小故障导致全产品无法安全维修，更小并不自动更好。

title: A River Walk with Notes
subtitle: 自然与观察 · 原创短文与原文定位
body: A school group visited the same stretch of river once a month and recorded visible changes, hoping that repeated observations would help students ask more precise questions about the place they usually passed without noticing. When the water looked darker after heavy rain, a student suggested pollution, but the teacher asked what other explanations might be possible before allowing a visual impression to become a conclusion about water quality. The group noted recent weather, nearby building work, and the location of fallen leaves, while learning that reliable claims about chemical contamination would require appropriate sampling and analysis rather than photographs of colour alone. Their display at school separated observations from possible explanations and unanswered questions, giving visitors a clearer picture of what the students had actually learned and what would still need further investigation by suitably trained people.
translation:
学校小组每月到同一河段记录可见变化，希望反复观察帮助学生对平时忽略的地方提出更具体问题。
暴雨后河水更暗，学生猜污染，老师要求先考虑其他解释，避免视觉印象直接成为水质结论。
小组记录天气、附近施工和落叶位置，并学习到化学污染判断需合适取样分析，不能只靠颜色照片。

title: A Classroom with Flexible Seats
subtitle: 学习与空间 · 原创短文与原文定位
body: A teacher replaced some fixed rows of desks with movable tables after noticing that students needed different arrangements for quiet reading, small discussions, and projects that required spreading materials across a larger shared surface. The class agreed on a few simple procedures for moving furniture, including keeping entrances clear and returning heavy tables with help, because flexibility would be less useful if changing the room created avoidable confusion or risk. Not every learner preferred working in a group, so the teacher preserved a quieter corner where students could complete individual tasks without being treated as less involved simply because they chose a different environment. The teacher judged the arrangement through classroom observation and student comments, rather than assuming that new furniture by itself would improve learning regardless of the tasks, instructions, and support provided during the lesson.
translation:
老师发现默读、小组讨论及铺开材料的项目需要不同布置后，把部分固定课桌换成移动桌。

title: An Exhibition of Ordinary Objects
subtitle: 文化与记忆 · 原创短文与原文定位
body: A local exhibition invited residents to lend ordinary household objects together with a short account of their meaning, suggesting that a worn cooking pot or a repaired umbrella could reveal stories absent from official photographs. One contributor brought a sewing box that had passed through three generations, while another offered a cheap plastic chair associated with long evenings when neighbours gathered outside during a period of building repairs. Curators photographed and labelled each item carefully, making clear which details came from the owner's memory and which could be confirmed through dated records, so that personal significance was not confused with independently verified history. The result encouraged visitors to notice objects they normally overlooked, without requiring every family to own something rare or expensive before its experiences could be considered worth recording and sharing with the wider community.

title: The Question behind a Search
subtitle: 数字与信息 · 原创短文与原文定位
body: When a student searched the web for the best way to study, she received confident advice pointing in several different directions, much of which did not explain what material had been learned or how success was measured. She made her question more specific by asking how to remember the meaning of unfamiliar words over several weeks, which helped her distinguish evidence about lasting recall from tips concerned mainly with feeling productive during a single afternoon. For each useful source, she noted who had written it, what kind of study it described, and whether its conclusions matched the actual results instead of relying only on a persuasive title or attractive illustration. The process did not give her a perfect method for every subject, but it produced a more careful starting point and a habit of checking what a recommendation could reasonably promise before making it part of her routine.
translation:
学生搜索最佳学习法时得到相互不同却很自信的建议，其中很多未说明材料或如何衡量成功。
她具体询问如何数周记住生词含义，这帮助区分长期回忆证据与主要让单个下午感觉高效的技巧。

这未给她各科完美方法，却带来谨慎起点与核查建议合理承诺的习惯，再把方法纳入日常。

title: A Market Moves Its Stalls
subtitle: 空间与服务 · 原创短文与原文定位
body: A weekend market attracted many visitors, yet its narrow central aisle became difficult to navigate whenever people stopped to compare products, leaving shoppers with pushchairs or walking aids struggling to pass through the busiest section. After observing the flow of people on two mornings, organisers moved larger displays away from the entrance and left space beside popular stalls so that customers could wait without blocking those who wanted to continue walking. Some sellers initially worried that a wider aisle would reduce the area available for their goods, but they agreed to a temporary arrangement when organisers promised to review the changes together rather than impose them permanently. The review considered both visitor comments and sellers' practical difficulties, recognising that a welcoming public space required attention to the people moving through it as well as those whose work depended on remaining in one place.

周末市场很热闹，但有人停下比较商品时，中央窄道就难走，推车或用助行器的顾客尤其难通过。
观察两早人流后，组织者把大展台移离入口，在热门摊旁留候等区，避免挡住要继续走的人。
一些摊主担心宽通道减少陈列区，但组织者承诺共同复盘而非永久强加后，同意暂时试行。
复盘兼顾顾客意见和摊主困难，认识到友好公共空间既需照顾流动的人，也需照顾靠固定摊位工作的人。

title: A Letter with One Clear Request
subtitle: 写作与沟通 · 原创短文与原文定位
body: A student wrote a long email to a course coordinator about a timetable problem, but the draft described so many background events that the reader would have struggled to identify what help was actually being requested. During revision, she placed the request near the beginning, explained the relevant conflict in two short paragraphs, and removed details that did not affect the decision the coordinator needed to make about her attendance. She also included the course code and the dates involved, while avoiding a claim that her preferred solution was the only reasonable one, since the coordinator might know of options she had not considered herself. The final message was still polite and personal, but its structure made it easier to answer, illustrating how clarity can come from selecting relevant information rather than simply shortening every sentence without regard to its purpose.
translation:
学生给课程协调人写很长邮件说课表问题，但背景太多，读者难辨究竟请求什么帮助。
修改时，她把请求放前面，两短段解释相关冲突，删掉不影响协调人决定出勤安排的细节。
她附课程代码和日期，也不声称偏好方案是唯一合理办法，因为协调人可能知道她未考虑的选项。
最终邮件仍礼貌亲切，但结构更便于答复，说明清晰来自选择相关信息，不只是无视目的地缩短每句。

questions.prompt: What was unclear in the first draft?

title: A Pocket Guide to a New Campus
subtitle: 校园与适应 · 原创短文与原文定位
body: A university welcome guide listed dozens of offices, yet new students often struggled to decide which one could help when a problem involved more than one service or did not match the formal name printed on a door. Student volunteers reorganised the guide around common situations, such as losing a card or needing a quiet place to join an online class, and included a general contact for questions that did not fit any category. They checked each entry with the office responsible, because a helpful-looking guide could become misleading if opening hours changed or a service moved to another building after the printed copies had already been distributed. A small web address on the back led to an updated version, while the paper guide remained useful for anyone whose phone was unavailable, showing that two formats could support different moments of the same student's day.

title: A Team Reviews a Failed Prototype
subtitle: 工程与迭代 · 原创短文与原文定位
body: When a student robot failed to carry a parcel across an uneven floor, the team initially blamed its small wheels, although the available video did not show clearly where the movement had first become unstable. They repeated the trial with one change at a time, keeping the parcel weight constant so that an improvement could be linked more reasonably to the feature being tested rather than to several simultaneous adjustments. A loose support beneath the platform turned out to be important, and tightening it reduced the shaking even before the wheels were replaced, reminding the team that a plausible first explanation still needed to be checked. Their report included the unsuccessful trials as well as the final design, because future students would learn more from knowing which ideas had been tested and rejected than from seeing only a polished photograph of the working machine.

学生机器人没能把包裹运过不平地面，团队先怪轮子小，但视频并未清楚显示最初哪里失稳。
他们一次只改一项并固定重量重复测试，使改善更合理地关联被测特征，而非多项同时变化。
平台下松支撑很关键，换轮前拧紧就减少摇晃，提醒团队初步解释即便合理仍需核查。

title: Making a Recipe Easier to Follow
subtitle: 信息与顺序 · 原创短文与原文定位
body: An online recipe attracted complaints from beginners who repeatedly discovered that an ingredient needed advance preparation only after they had already reached the step where it was supposed to be added to a hot pan. The writer revised the introduction to list equipment and preparation tasks before the cooking steps, while keeping detailed explanations nearby for readers who wanted to understand why a particular technique affected the texture of the finished dish. She also separated instructions that could happen simultaneously from those that depended on an earlier step, helping readers avoid leaving something unattended while searching through a long paragraph for the next essential action. A friend then tested the revised version without asking questions during the process, and the points where she hesitated became evidence for further edits rather than reasons to assume that she simply lacked common sense.

作者把器具和准备工作列在烹饪前，旁边保留详解，供想理解技法为何影响口感者阅读。
她区分可同时做与依赖前一步的指令，避免读者翻长段找关键动作时放任锅里东西无人看管。

title: The Smallest Useful Study Session
subtitle: 学习与坚持 · 原创短文与原文定位
body: On a day filled with classes and travel, a student found that the long study session planned the night before was no longer realistic, but she did not want the changed schedule to erase every opportunity to practise. She selected three previously studied phrases and tried to explain their meanings without opening her notes, then checked the examples and marked the one that still needed attention when a longer session became possible later. The short activity did not replace the reading and writing practice she had postponed, yet it gave her a clear place to resume instead of leaving an unfinished plan as a vague reminder of what had gone wrong. At the next planning moment, she adjusted the remaining work to fit her actual time rather than doubling the following day's tasks automatically, treating the record as information for a workable plan instead of a measure of personal worth.

课和出行占满的一天里，学生发现前夜计划的长学习段不现实，却不想失去所有练习机会。
她选三条学过的短语，先不看笔记解释，再核对例句，标出仍需关注的一条，留待以后较长学习。
短活动未替代推迟的读写，却给她明确续学点，不让未完成计划只成为模糊挫败提醒。
下次规划时，她按实有时间调整，不自动把次日任务翻倍，把记录当可行计划的信息而非个人价值量尺。

title: A Public Bench and a Simple Question
subtitle: 设计与体验 · 原创短文与原文定位
body: A town installed new benches that looked attractive in photographs, but an older resident asked why several had no backs or armrests when those features could make sitting down and standing up much easier for some visitors. The design team had focused on durability and appearance, which were legitimate concerns, yet it had not tested the seats with a sufficiently varied group of people before approving the final order for the public square. Rather than remove every bench immediately, the council added different seating options nearby and invited residents to comment on their use, recognising that one shape was unlikely to be comfortable for everyone who visited the same space. The discussion changed the next purchasing brief, which required practical trials as well as photographs, showing how a specific question about an everyday object could reveal whose experience had been missing from a seemingly complete design process.

title: A Volunteer Who Keeps Boundaries
subtitle: 服务与责任 · 原创短文与原文定位
body: A new volunteer at a community advice desk wanted to answer every question immediately, but she soon encountered requests involving housing disputes and complex forms that went beyond the information she had been trained to provide. Her supervisor explained that saying she needed to check was often more helpful than offering a confident guess, especially when a visitor might make an important decision based on what sounded like authoritative advice from the desk. The volunteer learned to record the essential question, identify the appropriate service, and explain the next step clearly, while asking permission before sharing a visitor's personal details with another organisation that might be able to help. She became more useful as she grew more aware of her limits, because a reliable handover could protect the visitor from misinformation and preserve the trust on which the wider community service depended for its everyday work.

title: When a Deadline Changes
subtitle: 计划与调整 · 原创短文与原文定位
body: A project team learned that its presentation date had moved forward by a week, forcing members to reconsider a plan in which research, drafting, and rehearsal had originally been arranged as separate stages with little overlap. Instead of asking everyone to work indefinitely longer hours, they identified the claims that required the strongest evidence and postponed decorative features that would make the slides look impressive without improving the audience's understanding of the central argument. Two members drafted different sections in parallel after agreeing on shared terms, while another checked the sources, and the team reserved one short rehearsal to discover gaps that would not be obvious from reading individual pages alone. The final presentation was simpler than initially imagined, but its essential claims were supported and its limitations were stated, illustrating that adjusting scope can sometimes be more responsible than maintaining an unrealistic promise about the amount of work delivered.
translation:
项目展示提前一周，团队不得不重想原本调研、写稿、排练分开且少重叠的计划。
他们未要求无限加时，而找出最需强证据的论点，推迟只好看却无助核心理解的装饰。
统一术语后，两人并行起草，另一人查来源，并保留短排练来发现单页阅读难见的缺口。

title: A Neighbourhood Sound Diary
subtitle: 声音与环境 · 原创短文与原文定位
body: Residents discussing street noise often disagreed because one person's quiet afternoon was another person's busiest working period, making a single description of the neighbourhood inadequate for explaining how sound affected people at different times of day. A local group invited volunteers to keep brief diaries noting when a sound occurred, what activity it interrupted, and whether it seemed temporary or repeated, without asking them to record private conversations or identify individual neighbours. The diaries showed that delivery hours and occasional building work created different problems, which helped participants discuss targeted changes rather than treating every uncomfortable sound as evidence that the entire street had become permanently unsuitable for living. Because the volunteers were not a representative sample and their notes were not calibrated measurements, the group presented the findings as descriptions of lived experience that could guide further investigation, not as a complete acoustic assessment of the area.
translation:
居民常因街噪争论，因为一人的安静下午可能是另一人的忙碌工作段，单一描述难解释不同时段影响。
小组请志愿者记声音时间、打断何事、临时还是反复，不要求录私人谈话或识别邻居。
日记显示送货时段与偶发施工造成不同问题，帮助针对性讨论，而非把所有不适声当整街永久不宜居证据。
志愿者不具代表性、笔记非校准测量，所以结果作为能引导后续调查的生活体验描述，而非完整声学评估。

Some families shared one old device, while others struggled with complicated forms or could not afford enough data, showing that a technical service may be available in principle without being equally usable in every household. The worker proposed measuring practical tasks alongside connection rates, such as whether people could submit an application or join a remote appointment, because those activities would reveal barriers hidden by a single impressive infrastructure statistic. Better equipment, clearer language, and accessible support would address different parts of the problem, so the report's authors added a section distinguishing the achievement of expanding the network from the continuing work of making participation genuinely possible.

title: An Online Course with a Stopping Point
subtitle: 学习与课程 · 原创短文与原文定位
body: A learner signed up for an online course whose lessons were all available immediately, but the freedom to watch anything at any time gradually turned into uncertainty about what she should do next and when she had done enough. She began choosing a small purpose before each session, such as explaining one concept or completing one worked example, and wrote a brief note about where to resume instead of treating the whole course as a single unfinished obligation. When a lesson was confusing, she could revisit its explanation or seek help, while a clear stopping point allowed her to leave the screen without pretending that watching another video would always be the most useful response to uncertainty. The resulting notes recorded questions and attempts as well as completed lessons, providing a more informative account of learning than the platform's viewing percentage alone could offer to someone trying to plan a realistic week.

学习者报名课程，所有课立即可看，但随时任选的自由渐变成不知下一步或何时足够的困惑。
每次前她选小目标，如解释一个概念或完成一例，并记续学处，不把整课当一个未完成义务。
遇难课可重看解释或求助，清楚停止点也让她能离屏，不假设再看一视频总是最好回应。

title: A Recommendation Is Not a Reason
subtitle: 技术与判断 · 原创短文与原文定位
body: An online bookstore recommended a novel to a reader because people with similar purchasing histories had bought it, but the reader wondered whether shared buying patterns meant that the book would address the questions she currently cared about. She read a sample chapter and several reviews that described the book's focus, separating comments about its writing style from those about its subject so that she could judge the recommendation against her own present purpose. The system remained useful for discovering titles she might otherwise miss, although its confident placement at the top of a page could not explain every aspect of the match between a particular text and an individual reader. Her final choice differed from the first suggestion, illustrating that personalised recommendations can provide starting points for exploration without replacing the reasons a person develops through reading, comparison, and reflection on what they actually need at the time.

title: An Archive That Needs Care
subtitle: 记录与保存 · 原创短文与原文定位
body: A community group scanned hundreds of photographs and felt that its history had been safely preserved, until one member asked who would maintain the files if the volunteer responsible for the shared account moved away. The group created a simple catalogue that connected each image to its description and permission record, while storing copies in more than one appropriate place instead of relying on a single device that could fail unexpectedly. They also agreed on who could add or change information, because an archive could lose value if dates were overwritten without explanation or personal details were shared more widely than the people in the photographs had expected. Preservation became an ongoing responsibility rather than a one-time scanning task, requiring occasional checks that files could still be opened and that the people managing access understood the commitments made when the material was first collected.

title: When Convenience Hides Work
subtitle: 劳动与服务 · 原创短文与原文定位
body: A campus delivery service promised effortless collection of groceries, but a student writing about the system noticed that convenience for customers depended on a sequence of tasks performed by people whose work was rarely visible in the advertisement. Orders had to be checked, bags packed, routes arranged, and failed deliveries resolved, while sudden changes in demand could make the same number of workers responsible for many more transactions within a limited period of available time. Rather than conclude that all delivery services were harmful, the student asked how schedules were set and how problems were handled, seeking information that would make it possible to discuss conditions rather than rely on assumptions about hidden effort. Her article explained the chain of work behind a simple button, encouraging readers to consider both the benefits of a useful service and the arrangements that made those benefits possible for the people receiving and providing it.

title: The Limits of an Average
subtitle: 统计与生活 · 原创短文与原文定位
body: A report stated that residents spent an average of thirty minutes travelling to work, which sounded manageable until a neighbourhood group asked how widely the actual journey times differed among people included in the calculation. Some workers lived close to their workplaces, while others changed buses twice and spent much longer on the road, so the average alone did not describe the daily experience of either group particularly well. The group requested additional information about the distribution of travel times and the reliability of services, arguing that an occasional long delay could matter greatly to someone whose working hours or childcare arrangements allowed little flexibility. The revised discussion still used the average as one summary measure, but placed it beside other evidence, demonstrating that a number can be accurate within its definition and yet incomplete as a guide to decisions affecting different lives.

有人住得近，有人换两次公交路上久，单靠平均值都无法很好描述两组日常。
小组要时长分布及服务可靠性，认为偶发大延误对工作或托育安排缺乏弹性的人影响很大。

title: A Reading Room Finds Its Purpose
subtitle: 公共服务与需求 · 原创短文与原文定位
body: A neighbourhood centre converted an unused office into a reading room, but attendance remained low even though the shelves were full and the furniture was comfortable, prompting staff to ask what residents actually needed from the space. Parents mentioned a place to wait between school collection and evening activities, while some workers wanted a quiet table for filling in forms, neither of which had been considered when the room was advertised mainly as a literary retreat. Staff changed the opening hours, added useful reference materials, and described the room through these ordinary situations, without removing the novels or requiring everyone who entered to justify how their visit related to serious reading and cultural participation. The room gradually served a wider range of purposes, reminding the centre that a well-equipped facility could still fail to meet local needs if its schedule and public description made those needs difficult to recognise or accommodate.

家长要放学接人至晚活动间等候处，工人要填表安静桌，这两点在主要宣传文学避静空间时都未考虑。
员工调整时间、加参考资料并用日常情境介绍，不撤小说，也不要求来访都证明与严肃阅读文化参与有关。

title: A Draft with Visible Changes
subtitle: 写作与反馈 · 原创短文与原文定位
body: After receiving feedback on an essay, a learner copied a polished model answer into a new document, but later realised that she could not explain which of her original choices had weakened the argument or why the replacement worked better. For the next assignment, she kept the first draft beside the revision and changed one paragraph at a time, writing a short reason whenever she added evidence, clarified a reference, or removed a sentence that did not support the main point. A tutor's suggestion remained something to evaluate rather than copy automatically, especially when the proposed wording sounded impressive but expressed a claim that went beyond the evidence the learner had actually included in the essay. The final version was not treated as the only successful outcome, because the record of decisions gave the learner material she could revisit when writing a different essay without the same tutor sitting beside her.

学习者收到作文反馈后抄范文，却发现说不清原来哪些选择削弱论证及新文为何更好。
下次她保留初稿与改稿并排，一段段改，每补证、澄清指代、删无关句时简记理由。

title: A Tool That Admits Uncertainty
subtitle: 人工智能与核查 · 原创短文与原文定位
body: A student used a text-generating tool to suggest explanations for a difficult paragraph, and the fluent response initially seemed reliable even though it included a claim that was not supported by anything in the passage she had provided. She asked the tool to identify the exact words behind each interpretation, then compared those references with the original text, discovering that one explanation relied on an assumption about the author rather than an observable detail within the paragraph. The tool still helped her generate questions and alternative paraphrases, but she treated these as drafts requiring judgement, particularly when they concerned subtle meanings that could change if a contrast word or a qualification was overlooked. Her notes separated the original sentence, her own interpretation, and the tool's suggestion, preserving a trace of how the answer had developed instead of presenting a fluent generated explanation as if it were an independently verified reading of the text.

title: Progress without a Public Scoreboard
subtitle: 学习与鼓励 · 原创短文与原文定位
body: A study group stopped displaying a weekly ranking after members said that comparing total hours did not reflect the different responsibilities, starting points, and kinds of practice that shaped what each person could reasonably do during the week. Instead, each learner kept a private record of completed attempts, questions that remained open, and examples of work they understood better than before, choosing whether to share any part of that record during a supportive conversation with another member. This change did not guarantee that everyone would study more or feel confident immediately, but it allowed encouragement to refer to something specific, such as a revised paragraph or a word recalled after an earlier mistake, rather than a public position. When someone returned after a difficult week, the group began with a manageable next step rather than a demand to repay missed hours, treating continuity as an opportunity to resume meaningful work instead of a competition to maintain an unbroken appearance.
translation:
学习组停止周榜，因为总时长比较没反映不同责任、起点和练习类型对每人一周可行任务的影响。
每人私记已做尝试、未解问题和比以前理解更好的例子，自选是否在互助谈话中分享。
改变不保证人人学更多或立即自信，但鼓励可指向改好一段或错后想起一词等具体表现，而非排名。
有人艰难一周后回来，小组从可行下一步开始，不催补欠时，把持续看作重接有意义工作机会，而非维持不断线外观的比赛。

title: A Translator Explains Revision
subtitle: 语言访谈 · 原创英语听力 · 合成语音
body: My first translation usually follows the source quite closely because I am trying to understand every part of it. The revision is where I ask whether the new reader can follow the same reasoning. Sometimes I divide a long sentence or repeat a noun where a pronoun would be unclear. That does not mean I am free to change the author's position. If the original says a result is possible, I should not turn it into a certainty simply because the stronger sentence sounds smoother. A useful translation preserves important distinctions while finding a natural way to express them for its intended audience.

questions.prompt: What does the translator focus on during revision?
options: Whether the new reader can follow the reasoning.
Keeping every pronoun regardless of clarity.

title: 请求调整一次预约
subtitle: 原创写作短练习 · 参考答案不唯一
body: 给写作中心写一封简短邮件：原预约与必修课冲突，提出一个替代时间，并表示可接受其他安排。先写完整初稿，再检查请求、原因、弹性是否清楚。
sample:
Dear Writing Centre,
I am writing to ask whether my appointment on Tuesday morning could be moved. A compulsory class has been rescheduled to the same time, so I would be unable to attend our meeting as planned. If possible, I would appreciate an appointment on Wednesday afternoon. However, I am happy to consider another available time. I have already prepared a draft and can send it before the appointment if that would be helpful. I apologise for any inconvenience and thank you for your assistance.
Best wishes,
Lin
analysis: 开头直接说请求，不让收件人从长背景里猜。
原因简明；could 和 would 让请求礼貌。
提供替代时间但不假设对方一定有空。
